question.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\cdot ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+0-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\  & =0, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
